title: Small monogram in surface embroidery
subtitle: A single initial worked in stem stitch on a linen piece
excerpt: A small monogram is the simplest first project in surface embroidery: one letter, worked in stem stitch, uses just the transfer and outline skills from the foundations sub-category.
heroPrompt: A small embroidered initial 'R' in dark navy stem stitch on white linen, inside a 10 cm wooden hoop, daylight, close-up.

content.text: A monogram initial is the best first project in surface embroidery because it uses only one stitch. Write the letter on fabric with a water-soluble pen, choose a thread colour, and follow the line in stem stitch. When it is done, the hoop is the frame.

items.label: Fabric
items.value: White or natural linen, 20 x 20 cm

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton in your chosen colour, 2 strands

content.text: Mount the linen in the hoop and tension it so it is firm and flat.
Print or write your chosen letter in a clear font at about 4 to 5 cm tall. Trace it onto the fabric with the water-soluble pen using a light box or window.
Thread the needle with 2 strands. Work stem stitch along every line of the letter, keeping the thread to the same side of the needle throughout.
On curves, shorten the stitch length slightly to follow the shape cleanly.
Once complete, dampen the fabric with a clean wet cloth to remove the water-soluble pen marks. Leave to dry in the hoop.
The finished piece can stay in the hoop as a display piece. Back the hoop with felt glued to the inner ring to finish the reverse.
